previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in left rib pain and nausea. Imaging showed no rib fracture, consistent with a rib contusion. Nausea, which occurred during dialysis, worsened with opioid use and improved after discontinuation and initiation of ranitidine. Visual hallucinations were reported and attributed to medication effects and chronic subdural fluid collections, which showed a slight interval increase on repeat CT; neurosurgery recommended clinical follow-up in one month. Right hip and foot pain following the fall were evaluated and found to be non-fracture-related, likely due to soft tissue injury or bursitis. The patient was discharged home with physical therapy services, with follow-up appointments scheduled in ophthalmology, rheumatology, neurosurgery, and nephrology, and no changes to most home medications except for adjustment in sevelamer and cinacalcet dosing.
problems: Nausea due to dialysis and opiates
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
